title: Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe
gist: Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 3.8 Live (and a 3.8 Live Extended Thinking variant claiming #1 on Artificial Analysis' speech-to-speech leaderboard) plus Gemini 3.5 Transcribe at 4.0% streaming WER, priced at $0.005/min audio in and $0.018/min audio out. The explicit pitch is that native speech-to-speech now replaces cascaded STT-LLM-TTS pipelines, with distribution routed through third-party media-infrastructure partners like LiveKit, Pipecat, Vercel and Agora.

insights.claim: Google is positioning native speech-to-speech models as a direct replacement for cascaded voice architectures (separate speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech stages), which would compress the value captured by vendors selling the individual pipeline stages.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Standalone STT/TTS vendors and orchestration middleware sitting between them face margin compression if end-to-end audio models win; watch whether voice-agent startups collapse their stacks onto a single model provider.
insights.quote: These models represent a step-change from our previous live models and provide a more streamlined alternative to cascaded architectures.
insights.locator: 3.8 Live Extended Thinking also supports configurable thinking

insights.claim: Gemini 3.8 Live is built to perform tool execution and dialogue simultaneously via asynchronous function calling, streaming audio to the user while API and tool calls run in the background — the core technical unlock for voice agents that do work rather than just talk.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Latency-masking during tool calls is the gating constraint for commercially usable voice agents in call centers and support; solving it opens labor-substitution use cases that text chat could not.
insights.quote: Execute API and tool calls in the background while continuing to stream audio responses to the user

insights.claim: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking supports configurable background reasoning that narrates its own progress mid-conversation, extending the test-time-compute trade-off from text into real-time voice where latency budgets are far tighter.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Configurable thinking in voice means per-call inference cost becomes a developer-tunable dial, making unit economics of voice agents variable rather than fixed.
insights.locator: 3.8 Live Extended Thinking also supports configurable thinking

insights.claim: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking is claimed to rank #1 on Artificial Analysis' Speech-to-Speech leaderboard, showing Google is now anchoring voice-model marketing to third-party benchmarks rather than internal evals.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Independent leaderboard leadership in speech-to-speech is a concrete competitive marker against OpenAI-style realtime voice APIs; track whether the ranking holds on the next release cycle.
insights.quote: 3.8 Live Extended Thinking delivers deeper reasoning, ranking #1 on Artificial Analysis’ Speech-to-Speech leaderboard.
insights.locator: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking

insights.claim: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe reports an average Word Error Rate of 4.0% streaming and 2.6% non-streaming across 85+ languages, putting streaming transcription accuracy within roughly 1.4 percentage points of batch accuracy.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: A small streaming-vs-batch accuracy gap removes the usual reason to run offline post-processing, so real-time captioning and live call analytics become deployable without a second pass.
insights.quote: it achieved an average Word Error Rate (WER) of 4.0% (streaming) and 2.6% (non-streaming)
insights.locator: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe: Our dedicated speech-to-text model

insights.claim: Alphanumeric precision — accurately parsing confirmation codes, claim numbers, and technical data — is called out as a distinct capability, signaling that the target market is regulated transactional workflows like insurance claims and support desks rather than casual chat.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Alphanumeric reliability is the specific failure mode that has kept voice AI out of insurance, banking and airline support; if solved, those BPO budgets become addressable.
insights.quote: Accurately parse confirmation codes, claim numbers, and technical data

insights.claim: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe lets developers bias recognition toward domain terms by passing a custom_vocabulary list of up to 1,000 terms, plus automatic handling of intra-sentence code-switching without manual configuration.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Domain vocabulary biasing and automatic code-switching are the two features enterprises previously bought specialist ASR vendors for; bundling them into a frontier model erodes that niche.
insights.quote: by passing a custom_vocabulary list of up to 1,000 terms

insights.claim: Gemini Live audio is priced at $0.005 per minute for audio input and $0.018 per minute for audio output, meaning output audio costs roughly 3.6x input and a continuous hour of two-way voice runs on the order of a dollar or less in model cost.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: At these per-minute rates, model cost falls far below human agent cost per call minute, which is the arithmetic that drives contact-center displacement; the input/output asymmetry also rewards designs that listen more than they speak.
insights.quote: Competitively priced at $0.005/min for audio input and $0.018/min
insights.locator: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking are available

insights.claim: Google is routing voice-model distribution through named media-infrastructure partners — Agora, Fishjam, LiveKit, LangChain, Pipecat, Vercel and Vision Agents — outsourcing the hard streaming plumbing rather than building it in-house.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: These partners become the toll booths for enterprise voice deployment; being on Google's integration list is a durable demand signal for LiveKit, Pipecat and Agora-type businesses.
insights.quote: our Live API integration partners that handle media streaming infrastructure for real-world deployment
insights.locator: Developers can also access the models through Agora

insights.claim: The audio suite is being sold as a full stack rather than single models, spanning Gemini 3.5 Live Translate (speech-to-speech translation across 70+ languages), Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS for configurable speech generation, and Lyria 3.5 for production-grade music generation.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: Bundling translation, TTS and music generation behind one API raises switching costs for developers and squeezes point solutions in each of those categories.
insights.locator: Our complete audio suite for developers

insights.claim: Multilingual coverage differs by model tier — 97+ languages for the Live speech-to-speech models versus 85+ for the dedicated Transcribe model — indicating end-to-end audio models now surpass the dedicated ASR model on language breadth.
insights.speaker: Alisa Fortin
insights.so_what: If the general model already outruns the specialist model on coverage, the long-term product roadmap points toward collapsing the dedicated ASR SKU entirely.
insights.quote: Reach global audiences with coverage for 97+ languages and accent consistency
